_readme: Keyword -> DM card config. Data-driven and separate from code: the cron is dumb, the data varies.
SCHEMA v2 (2026-08-31). Restructured so a small UI tool can create and edit entries later
WITHOUT a human or Claude reading prose to work out an entry's real state. Every fact the
system acts on is now its own field; `notes` is commentary ONLY and nothing reads it.
id              STABLE UNIQUE identity. Never reuse, never rename - it is the utm_campaign,
and renaming it orphans every click already recorded in GA4 under the old one.
keyword         the SPOKEN word, i.e. what the reel's audio tells viewers to comment. NOT an
identity: two entries may legitimately share one (LABEL), which is exactly why
`id` exists as a separate field.
aliases         extra words that also trigger this entry.
match           'word' (default, word-boundary) or 'contains'.
enabled         whether this entry can fire.
blocked_reason  WHY it is off, in one line, or null. A UI shows this instead of parsing notes.
media_ids       pins the entry to specific posts. An ENABLED entry with an EMPTY list is
unscoped and answers its word on ANY post carrying any CTA - never do that.
extra_media_ids HAND-PINNED posts this entry also answers, which sync_media_ids.py NEVER adds
to or removes. Use it when a post is genuinely served by an entry that did not
produce it - e.g. an Evergreen carousel whose CTA is LABEL, where the guide is
the right answer even though the post is not that reel. Deliberate, and
survives every re-sync; `media_ids` is derived and does not.
pieces          MACHINE-READABLE list of the content pieces this entry serves, e.g.
['SCR-08','SCR-09']. This is what pins media_ids: sync_media_ids.py maps each
posted Instagram post to a piece via Notion's `Source File` path, then to the
entry that claims that piece. Empty list = pin by hand (e.g. the product page).
source_piece    the same thing in human form, for reading. NOTHING acts on it.
url             the blog article, WITH its three UTMs.
title/subtitle/button_title/image_url   the DM card itself.
pdf             the guide the blog page serves.
blog_attribute  the page's data-guide-download value, where it has one (may differ from id).
notes           free prose. Commentary only - NOTHING in the code reads this.
utm_campaign == id. Format: <keyword-slug>-<piece-code>, so anyone reading a GA4 report can see
both the offer and which content piece it came from: label-scr04 vs label-scr07, bingo-rtl07,
myth-sst12. The three UTMs are source/medium/campaign ONLY - the site is configured for three,
so the content identifier goes INSIDE the campaign (Pritam, 2026-08-31).
AUTHORITY (fixed 2026-08-31): the keyword is whatever the REEL'S RECORDED AUDIO says.
The caption files (...\SCRIPT N Captions\SCRNN_CAPTIONS.md) hold those decisions and win over
lead_magnets\INDEX.md, which is older and still lists three superseded words.
SCR-08 + SCR-09 -> 'OLD IS GOLD' (not DADA / DADI)   - Pritam 2026-08-04
SCR-13          -> 'KIDS'        (not BACHCHA)       - Pritam 2026-08-04
SCR-07          -> 'LABEL'       (SACH is retired)   - Pritam 2026-08-08
LANDING PAGES (2026-08-31): ManyChat is NOT used at all. The DM button sends people to a
dietswad.in BLOG PAGE, and the blog page carries the PDF download button. So `url` is always
a blog article, never a Drive link and never a raw PDF. Blog status lives in
..\..\Development studio\website-revamp\BLOG_PROGRESS.md.
